what: The CSS Clip Path Generator cuts an element into a shape, such as a triangle, star, arrow, hexagon or circle, and writes the clip-path CSS for it. You can drag every corner point on the preview to make your own shape.
It is useful for web designers who want angled section edges, shaped images, badges and decorative elements without editing images.
You can preview the shape on your own image; the image stays on your device.
uses: Show a photo as a hexagon, circle or star.
Use Slanted edge to give a page section a diagonal bottom.
Make arrow, chevron and message-bubble shapes from a plain div.
Copy two clip-paths with the same number of points and animate between them with a CSS transition.
Drag, add and remove points to trace any outline you need.
tutorial: Click a shape button. Polygon shapes show white dots at each corner; circle and ellipse show a center dot; inset uses sliders.
Drag a dot to move that corner. The faint image behind shows the full element, so you can see what is cut away. Snap to whole percent keeps numbers tidy.
Tap a dot to select it, then use the arrow keys to move it by 1%, or 5% with Shift.
Add point inserts a new corner halfway along the edge after the selected point. Remove selected point deletes it; a polygon needs at least three.
Use the Radius sliders for circle and ellipse, and the Top, Right, Bottom, Left and Corner round sliders for inset.
Choose a preview background or My own image, then click Copy CSS. The code includes a -webkit- line for older Safari versions.
features: Triangle, trapezoid, parallelogram, rhombus, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, star, arrow, chevron, cross, message, slanted edge, circle, ellipse and inset.
Works with mouse, touch and keyboard.
Preview the clip on a picture from your device without uploading it.
Percent values, so the shape scales with the element, plus a -webkit- prefixed line.

example.title: Worked example: an angled hero section
example.text: Click Slanted edge. The code is polygon(0% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 80%, 0% 100%): the right side ends at 80% of the height and the left side at 100%, giving a diagonal bottom edge. Drag the bottom-right point up to 70% for a steeper angle, then paste the clip-path line into the CSS of your hero section.

tips: Percent values make the shape follow the element's size, so the same code works on phones and desktops.
Content outside the shape is cut off, including text and shadows; add padding so text stays inside.
box-shadow is clipped too. Use filter: drop-shadow() on a parent element to shadow a clipped shape.
To animate between two polygons, they must have the same number of points.
problems: Check that the element has a size and a background, and that no other rule sets clip-path: none.
It lies outside the shape. Add padding or move the points outward.
Percent values follow the element's width and height. Give the element a fixed aspect ratio, for example aspect-ratio: 1, to keep shapes like stars regular.
Only image files can be used. If the file is a PDF or document, convert it to JPG or PNG first.
